policy: Transform the imported photograph while preserving its head-and-shoulders framing, pose, outfit and natural facial proportions. Never invent unseen bodies or poses from the style reference. Use a model only when the target medium needs a new portrait; keep native filters for photographic treatments.

nativeTreatments.treatment: Editable rose filter, eye crop and graphics. No generated portrait.

studies.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve portrait editing with restrained pixel-art style transfer.
Input image 1 is the original photograph of Railly Hugo. His exact facial identity and proportions are the priority. Input image 2 is the original IA Hackathon badge and supplies only the grayscale palette, technical mood and pixel-art medium, NEVER the other person's face or simplified anatomy.
Create a handsome, natural editorial BUST PORTRAIT of the exact adult man in image 1, translated into fine, carefully drawn grayscale pixel art. Reproduce his actual facial structure: long oval face, natural narrow cheekbones, small ears, exact eye size and spacing, his nose and relaxed closed lips, thick but naturally proportioned eyebrows, short chin beard and the same short spiky dark hair silhouette. Preserve his real head-to-neck ratio and calm serious expression. Use the photograph's existing pose and light direction. Do not invent a different man.
Medium: refined 16-bit portrait illustration with subtle small pixel clusters and at least 16 distinct gray values, approximately 160 to 200 effective pixels across the whole portrait. Keep anatomical forms realistic with nuanced cheek, eye socket and jaw shading. Crisp square pixel steps in the silhouettes and hair, quiet carefully controlled dithering in the shadows. It should feel like an editorial photograph reconstructed by an expert pixel artist. No cartoon facial outline and no flat white face. No enlarged eyes, exaggerated ears, compressed midface, big head, toy anatomy, mascot, chibi, anime or game NPC caricature.
Square 1024 by 1024 composition: original haircut fully visible with about 7% headroom; face and upper shoulders dominate; eyes near 39% image height, chin near 68%; black crewneck shirt at the bottom with visible soft graphite-gray folds. Bust only, no waist, arms, hands or legs. Even charcoal background #090a0b. Gentle rim light separates the black hair from the background. Balanced facial contrast, natural grayscale skin with tonal detail.
Output ONLY this portrait image. No badge frame, UI, grid, lettering, numbers, event name, QR code, logos, border, watermark or other people. All badge layout and materials are composited separately by the editor.

Use case: style-transfer with identity-preserve. Asset type: a standalone portrait layer for Badge Studio. Input image 1 is Railly Hugo, the ONLY identity to depict. Preserve his recognizable face proportions, short spiky dark hair, thick eyebrows, dark eyes, nose, lips and short chin beard. Input image 2 shows an original event badge of another person: use it ONLY for art direction, never copy that person's identity. Produce a newly rendered portrait of Railly in the specified medium. No text, numbers, labels, logos, borders, frames, QR, lanyard or extra people. The editor draws the badge composition separately. Output ONLY the portrait asset.
Match the Next Craft reference's large, expressive monochrome pixel portrait. Deliberate chunky square pixel clusters, about 96 pixels across the face, 8 to 12 gray values, softly warm bone highlights, near-black shadows. This is carefully drawn pixel illustration, not a nearest-neighbor downsized photo, not a cartoon sprite body. Straight-on head and upper chest, spiky haircut fully visible, relaxed expression, plain black crewneck shirt from image 1. Preserve Railly's exact facial proportions in the new medium. Square canvas, head centered, top of hair at 8% image height, chin at 68%, shoulders spread across the bottom edge, wide enough to leave background around hair. Flat background exactly #1a1a17, no texture baked into it. Crisp pixel edges. Do not transfer glasses, smile, curly hair or full beard from the style reference.

Use case: identity-preserve editing of the supplied photo into fine pixel art.
Input image 1 is the ONLY edit target and the ONLY identity reference: Railly Hugo's original square head-and-shoulders photograph. Input image 2 is an original Vibecode Fest badge belonging to a different person and supplies ONLY the grayscale pixel-art treatment, never its composition, pose, clothing or person.
EDIT IMAGE 1 IN PLACE conceptually: preserve its exact crop, head scale, face placement, camera angle, gaze, serious expression, hairstyle, face anatomy, black crewneck shirt and visible shoulder silhouette. Convert the existing photographic forms into finely illustrated grayscale pixel clusters and restrained dithering. Do not recompose or extend the photograph. Do not add a body or invent a pose. No arms, crossed arms, hands, waist, legs, feet or extra clothing. Show ONLY what is visible in the original photo.
Preserve the original adult man's long oval face, exact natural eye size and spacing, small ears, slim nose, relaxed lips, thick natural eyebrows, short chin beard and short spiky dark haircut. The likeness and natural proportions take priority over stylization. This is a finely reconstructed 1990s grayscale desktop portrait, not a cartoon character, chibi, mascot, anime or blocky game avatar. Approximately 160 to 200 effective pixels across the portrait with at least 16 gray shades, thin pixel contours and delicate dithering; retain facial tonal detail.
Square 1024 by 1024 image. Match the input photo's head-and-shoulders framing: full hair visible near the top, eyes near 43% image height, shoulders and the same black crewneck shirt at the bottom. Keep the face dominant. Replace only the original backdrop with pure white #ffffff, no floor or shadow. The editor will remove this white background and place the head-and-shoulders cutout over its own checkerboard.
No badge, sky, grass, window, icons, UI, checkerboard, borders, text, numbers, logo, QR code, watermark or extra people. Output the transformed original portrait ONLY. Never borrow the folded-arm pose or half-body composition from input image 2.

Use case: identity-preserve portrait editing with fine pixel-art style transfer.
Input image 1 is Railly Hugo's original photograph and defines the EXACT identity, face proportions, pose and crop. Input image 2 is an original HACK0.DEV Christmas badge: use it ONLY as a reference for colorful pixel-art technique and festive palette. Do not copy the other person's face, body or clothing.
Recreate ONLY the original head-and-shoulders photograph in refined, expressive, colorful pixel art. Keep the same adult face, natural eye size and spacing, face shape, slim nose, relaxed lips, thick natural eyebrows, short chin beard, short spiky dark hair and black crewneck shirt. Preserve the original camera angle, calm expression and original head-to-shoulder proportions. No invented body: do not draw waist, arms, hands, legs or feet. Do not turn him into a game character, mascot, chibi, doll or caricature. No enlarged eyes or oversized head.
Use fine deliberate square pixel clusters, approximately 160 to 200 effective pixels across the whole portrait, nuanced warm skin-tone shading, detailed dark hair, rich but restrained Christmas red, cream and deep green accents. Retain the recognizable face anatomy from input 1. The medium is carefully illustrated pixel art, with natural portrait proportions and subtle dithering, not a crude low-resolution avatar or a blurry filter.
A small red Santa hat with cream trim may rest naturally on the top of his head, leaving the distinctive hairline and some spiky hair visible. Keep his original black shirt. Do not invent a sweater or outfit. The face stays dominant, with complete head and comfortable headroom, eyes near 42% image height, shoulders extending across the lower edge. Square 1024 by 1024 canvas, a close bust composition matching input 1. Uniform background exactly #153b33; no floor, scene or cast shadow. Gentle warm light retains skin detail without clipping.
Output ONLY this portrait. No text, numbers, logos, title, border, badge frame, garlands, ornaments, QR, watermark or extra people. The editor provides the winter material, animated snow, typography and metadata separately.

postprocessing: Lossless WebP. Edge-connected background removal for Vibecode and Christmas only; no cropping or body reconstruction. Winter portrait filter is original to preserve generated color.
rejected: Initial IA caricature and its bust crop, full-body Christmas, folded-arm Vibecode and generated She Ships are archived locally and removed from public assets.
